To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the prevalence of HCV infection is high among the HIV-infected population, 2) HIV infection is a risk factor for HCV infection and 3) HCV infection in HIV-infected individuals is associated with an increase in mortality.

the HCV/HIV co-infection is a serious health problem in Tunisia.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the results of our study show that HCV infection is a significant public health problem among the HIV-positive population in Tunisia, and that HCV-HIV-coinfected patients are more likely to have a history of injection drug use, to be older, and to be more likely to be infected with the HCV genotype 1 than HIV-monoinfected patients.
the HCV-HIV co-infection rate in Tunisia is higher than in other countries.
the HCV-HIV-coinfected population in Tunisia was characterized by a high rate of HCV infection and a high prevalence of HIV infection.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HCV-HIV-coinfection is associated with a higher prevalence of liver disease, and that the prevalence of liver disease is higher in HIV-infected patients with HCV-HIV than HIV monoinfection.
